content.title: Recap: Hornets extend win streak to 5 to highlight Thursday
content.text: Kon Knueppel becomes the only player age-22 or younger in NBA history to sink 250 made 3-pointers in a single season. Copyright 2026 NBAE (Photo by Kent Smith/NBAE via Getty Images) Check out the best of Thursday’s three-game slate with the NBA.com live blog, featuring all of the meaningful moments, performances, observations, news, notes and highlights. 2026 Playoff Picture: Where teams stand NBA commissioner Adam Silver on league’s plan to explore expansion Last night’s live blog: Wolves complete NBA’s largest OT comeback Download the NBA App What we know after Thursday night’s games: Jalen Duren became the first player in Pistons franchise history to record at least 30 points, 10 rebounds and 5 assists while shooting 80% or better from the field during their 129-108 win over New Orleans. Kon Knueppel is the only player age-22 or younger in NBA history to make 250 3-pointers in a single season. He led the Hornets with 26 points (6 3PM), 11 rebounds and 8 assists to help Charlotte win their fifth straight while snapping New York’s seven-game win streak in the process. Orlando snapped their six-game losing streak with a close 121-117 victory against the Kings. Paolo Banchero (30 pts, 9 reb, 7 ast) tallied his third straight outing with at least 30 points. Jalen Duren dropped 26 points and 14 rebounds in Detroit’s 130-129 OT loss to Atlanta last night. Mandatory Credit: Stephen Lew-Imagn Images Two of the hottest teams in the league meet tonight when LaMelo Ball and the Hornets welcome Jalen Brunson and the Knicks to Buzz City (7 ET, NBA TV). Charlotte has won four straight and 22 of their last 28 games dating back to Jan. 22, while New York has strung together seven consecutive victories and are 13-4 over their last 17 contests. Our John Schuhmann has more details behind Charlotte’s historic turnaround. On League Pass, the New Orleans Pelicans visit the East-leading Detroit Pistons for an interconference showdown (7 ET), and the Orlando Magic host the Sacramento Kings in hopes of snapping their season-long six-game losing streak (7 ET).
